decisions.reason: The prior exclusivity attribute reserves the expressive right-arm signature to the Hero V and É accent, but the source explicitly gives the optically drawn second V an extended right-arm signature matched to the Hero V.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
After reviewing these explorations for a while and revisiting the previous proofs, I think I now understand what has been troubling me. Continuing to scale the second V mathematically does not seem to be the solution.

Although the smaller V is technically a true proportional reduction, it feels as though it comes from another alphabet. It loses part of the character and presence that make the Hero V so powerful.

I’d prefer to reset the work around our original Hero V, which I still consider the strongest version we have developed. From that starting point, I’d like to investigate a second V that is designed optically instead of being mechanically reduced. It should share the same DNA and feel native to the same alphabet while naturally serving in a supporting role. I would retain the extended right arm as our signature detail and match it optically to the Hero V, but I’d rather achieve that by drawing it than through pure scaling. I’m attaching my current favorite image, though that version does not include the right-arm extension.

I believe this direction will produce a more unified and timeless wordmark, with every letter appearing deliberately crafted rather than mechanically generated.

value_updates.signature_exclusivity: The É accent retains the Hero V's literal expressive right-arm signature; the second V may carry an optically drawn extended-right-arm signature matched to the Hero V, while the gesture remains excluded from the E and L.
